status: Locally verified source fix after published 0.13.0. No new archive, release or production deployment. Full AgentOS parity remains open.
problem: A root entering child wait, poll or stopped state after admission could schedule its next one-second wake beyond the 30-second execution lease. With exact native virtual-time advancement, the delivery then had no due wake and the native Queue returned exception, leaving the receipt running rather than checkpointed.

diagnosis.rejectedHypothesis: An uninterruptible semaphore waiter blocking family scope closure was initially suspected. Instrumentation showed handover/scope closure had not started. Timestamped root wait observations proved the relative-sleep overshoot; no semaphore or scope lifetime change was made.
diagnosis.previousWorkaround: The earlier source proof waited for completed setup stdout before advancing time. That readiness option, Schema import/field, native JSON binding, global Env field and sole caller are removed in this cutover. The clock now advances after the first acknowledged output for every workload.

change: One absolute handoverAt deadline owns the existing 30-second lease. Eligible root stopped/child-wait/poll paths cap each requested sleep by the remaining lease and the existing observation bound. Guest clock and capability-expiry bounds retain their meanings. A poll can immediately recheck an expired lease instead of forcing another one-millisecond delay. Fuel thresholds, process grants, persisted deadlines, Semaphore behavior and checkpoint formats are unchanged.

before.source: Original src/wasi.ts from 2b7c35b, with identical new fixture/test sources and the first-output clock driver.
failures: foreground-family delivery returned native Queue exception
delayed canonical read delivery returned native Queue exception

verification.boundary: The delayed fixtures perform a real 20-millisecond WASI clock poll before entering an indefinite read or signal stop. All PTY and blocked-family lease checkpoints assert savedAt equals the original start plus the same 30,000-millisecond advance.
verification.retention: Replacement Workers use real native R2 checkpoints and original grants/deadlines. Parent/child handles, selected foreground, partial canonical input, stopped parent/continued child, buffered bytes and EOF retain exact results. Stale Queue delivery preserves terminal receipts and output without reentry. Existing synced/unsynced filesystem handover tests also pass.
verification.cleanup: All DEBUG-handover instrumentation was removed. No timeout was increased and the original failing foreground flow runs without a setup readiness gate.

generalBenchmark.limits: Maintained local regression workload; no paired baseline, production latency or billing claim. Existing performance evidence was preserved.

limits: Local native workerd/R2/Queue with request-local Effect TestClock; no new production incident or production timing proof is claimed.
Requested sleeps respect the deadline; platform scheduling and outstanding native I/O can still delay actual execution.
These cases close the reproduced admission-time scheduling defect, not every possible interruption, arbitrary-crash or cross-build recovery case.
Remote CI, matching archives and production delivery of this source fix remain separate gates.
